wave: CORRECTNESS -- a single unreadable FILE (distinct from the already-fixed unreadable-DIRECTORY case) still aborted the whole source-tree walk
wave_title: The immediately preceding generation (10d1576a4) fixed `visit_inventory`'s `fs::read_dir(dir)?` so an unreadable DIRECTORY no longer aborts the walk. `visit_inventory`'s per-entry classification still called `classify_file(root, &path)?` unconditionally -- and `classify_file` itself calls `fs::metadata(path)?` and (via `looks_binary`) `File::open(path)?`, either of which returns `Err` for a permission-denied or vanished FILE. That `?` still propagated straight out of `visit_inventory`, aborting the whole source-tree walk for one unreadable file, the exact same defect class one level of granularity finer than the directory case just fixed.

generation_model.G_n: 10d1576a43 (fix(adapter): an unreadable directory no longer aborts the whole walk) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Direct continuation of the immediately preceding generation's own falsification method, narrowed from a directory to a file: constructed a real scratch repository (via the non-root `ubuntu` account, since root bypasses the permission checks this class of bug depends on -- the same rigor already established) with one ordinary readable `.rs` file and one `chmod 000` `.rs` file, committed with git (permissions set AFTER commit, since git itself refuses to `add` an unreadable file -- confirming this is a realistic post-checkout scenario, e.g. a build step or another process locking a file down after checkout, not merely a synthetic one). Reproduced the crash cleanly against the code as it stood immediately after the directory-level fix: `atlas-systemizer: <root>: Permission denied (os error 13)`, zero stdout -- proving the directory-level fix, while real and necessary, had not closed the class completely.

priority_classification: correctness / hostile-and-degraded-environment handling (priority 1/2) -- the fifth instance this session of the same defect class (one artifact's io::Error aborting the entire pipeline), now closed at the finest remaining granularity (one file) for the source-tree walker specifically.

design_decisions.question: Patch each of `entry.file_type()`, `classify_file`, `classify_non_file`'s call sites individually inside the loop (mirroring the directory-level fix's per-call-site `match`), or restructure once?
design_decisions.decision: Restructure once: extracted the whole per-entry classification decision into a new `classify_entry(root, entry, out) -> io::Result<Option<ArtifactRecord>>`, called from `visit_inventory`'s loop through a single `match` that recovers from ANY `Err` it returns (whichever of the three internal calls produced it) via the same `record_unreadable_artifact` helper the directory fix introduced -- renamed from `record_unreadable_directory` since it's now generically about any inaccessible path, not directories specifically. This closes the whole per-entry failure surface in one place rather than requiring three near-identical recovery blocks (one per internal call site), and means a future fourth internal call added to entry classification is protected automatically rather than needing its own bespoke recovery to be remembered.

design_decisions.question: What `ArtifactKind`/`ArtifactDisposition` to record for an unreadable FILE, given `entry.file_type()` may itself be what failed (so we may not even know whether it was a file, directory, or symlink)?
design_decisions.decision: `ArtifactKind::Special`/`ArtifactDisposition::Unknown` -- the same pair the directory case uses, and for the same reason: `Unknown` precisely means 'we cannot determine what this artifact actually is/contains', which is exactly true whether `entry.file_type()`, `fs::metadata`, or `File::open` was the call that failed. Using `ArtifactKind::File` would overclaim a fact (that we successfully determined it IS a regular file) the failure may not have actually established.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: A single file this process cannot classify -- because it cannot be stat'd, cannot be opened for its binary-detection sniff, or its directory-entry type cannot be determined -- anywhere in a repository's source tree no longer aborts `systemize`/`code_analyze`/`check`/`parse`/`work prepare`. It is recorded as an explicit `ArtifactRecord` (kind `SPECIAL`, disposition `UNKNOWN`, reason naming the real OS error) rather than silently dropped, and every other artifact in the repository is still inventoried normally.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: New `#[cfg(unix)]` regression test `an_unreadable_file_is_recorded_not_classified_and_does_not_abort_the_rest_of_the_tree` in `adapter/src/source/mod.rs`, using a real `chmod 000` file, guarded by the same root-detection skip introduced for the directory-level test in the immediately preceding generation.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: Real, rebuilt `atlas-systemizer` binary invoked as the non-root `ubuntu` account against a scratch repository with one `chmod 000` `.rs` file: previously `exit 2`, 'Permission denied (os error 13)', zero stdout; now `exit 0`, correctly listing `Cargo.toml`/`src/lib.rs` as parsed while recording `src/locked.rs` as `{"kind": "SPECIAL", "disposition": "UNKNOWN", "reason": "artifact-not-accessible: Permission denied (os error 13)"}`. Full workspace re-run (`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`) and a fresh `systemize` run against the real Atlas-Studio repository itself confirm zero regression to any existing gate, blocker, or test.

implementation.adapter/src/source/mod.rs: `record_unreadable_directory` renamed to `record_unreadable_artifact` (generalized: it now records any inaccessible path, not directories specifically; reason prefix changed from `directory-not-readable:` to `artifact-not-accessible:`). New `classify_entry` function extracts the per-entry classification decision (`entry.file_type()`/`classify_file`/`classify_non_file`) out of `visit_inventory`'s loop into its own `io::Result<Option<ArtifactRecord>>`. `visit_inventory`'s loop now matches on `classify_entry`'s result, recovering via `record_unreadable_artifact` on any `Err` instead of propagating it. New falsification-first regression test.

overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED AND VERIFIED. A single unreadable file anywhere in a repository's source tree previously aborted the entire pipeline with zero report -- the file-level sibling of the directory-level defect fixed in the immediately preceding generation, discovered by directly continuing that generation's own falsification method one level finer. Fixed by extracting per-entry classification into `classify_entry` and recovering uniformly from any failure path through the same `record_unreadable_artifact` helper (now generalized rather than directory-specific), with the unreadable file explicitly accounted for (never silently dropped). Verified with a real, non-root, falsification-first end-to-end reproduction plus a root-detection-guarded unit regression test, with zero regression to the real repository's own state or any existing test.
